newsitem.title: USA: HORSE RACING-RAIN MAY PRODUCE OFF TRACK FOR KENTUCKY DERBY.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-RAIN MAY PRODUCE OFF TRACK FOR KENTUCKY DERBY.

text.p: Forecasters on Friday predicted overnight rain storms that could produce an off track for the 123rd running of the $1 million Kentucky Derby at Churchill Downs, an outlook that could help outsiders in the race.

"The rain could help the California horses," injured jockey Chris McCarron said during morning exercises. McCarron had been scheduled to ride Irish-bred Hello, but a shoulder injury forced him out of America's most famous horse race.

From his vantage point on the sidelines, he said he saw a race shaping up where the three California runners - Free House, Silver Charm and Hello - set the early pace with favoured Pulpit and second-favourite Captain Bodgit waiting for the homestretch of the 1 1/4-mile race to make their move.

Weather forecasters called for rain beginning late Friday and continuing overnight into the morning of Saturday's racing. If that forecast holds, by the time the Derby goes off, the track could be "cuppy," a drying mud that slows the pace.

Most of the horses in the race have been successful on off-tracks but observers said a muddy surface could favour such horses as Captain Bodgit, a 5-2 second favourite in the morning line and winner in the slop at the Wood Memorial, and Hello, who has experience running on turf in England.

McCarron was replaced by Mike Smith on Hello, which had a short run Friday morning and was declared fit and ready by trainer Ron McAnally. "He's a very nice horse to ride," McCarron said, "very generous."

Another horse with a win over an off-track is Concerto, who won at Churchill Downs last year on a sloppy surface. His owner, New York Yankee boss George Steinbrenner, is looking for a rare U.S. sports double -- a World Series and a Kentucky Derby.

The rotund Steinbrenner, who was out early to watch final preparations, declared the Derby "the greatest two minutes in sports." And he warned fans not to rule out his horse, which was listed at 8-1 on the early line.
"I always knew this was a good horse. This guy has a mountain of heart," he said of Concerto, which has won seven of 10 races, including three graded stakes.

A field of 13 was set for the race, the smallest number of entries since 1985. The last Derby raced in bad weather was the 1994 "Run for the Roses" when McCarron won aboard Go for Gin at 9-1 on a sloppy track.
